crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are the structured grids that turn individual research reports into comparable rows and columns for a literature review or evidence synthesis.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus is the practice of assessing how much agreement actually exists across a body of research, rather than assuming that a large number of papers equals a settled finding.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the habit of auditing the evidence base of a review you are writing or have already published, rather than trusting the citations you have accumulated.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans cover the use of autonomous or semi-autonomous software to plan, run and report on broad literature searches.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines in evidence synthesis means making concepts, measures, and findings from one field legible to another without flattening their meaning.

sections.body: Literature review and evidence synthesis is the work of turning a pile of papers into a defensible account of what is known. In practice, AI systems now read full texts and pull out claims, methods, sample sizes and results into structured tables, which is the part of the job that used to consume most of a reviewer's time. They cluster findings by theme, flag where studies agree or conflict, and draft the first pass of a synthesis that a human then checks. This site's library holds 295 research papers and 14104 claims extracted from research works, which gives a sense of the scale these tools are built to handle. The output is a map of the evidence, not a verdict, and the reviewer still owns the interpretation.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Extraction is largely solved for clearly written papers with standard structures, and it is reliable enough to save real hours on a first pass. Weighing consensus is harder, because agreement in the literature is not the same as agreement in the world, and models tend to overstate confidence when abstracts are emphatic and methods sections are thin. Questioning your own sources is the least automated part, since it requires knowing what a study could not have shown, and no current system does that reliably on its own. Deep research agents can scan a field broadly and return a structured overview, but they miss paywalled work, misread tables, and sometimes cite papers that do not support the sentence attached to them. The honest limit is that synthesis still needs a person who can tell a strong study from a weak one.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the arc of a review. Evidence Extraction Tables covers the mechanical stage, pulling claims and numbers out of papers into something comparable, and it is where most readers start. Weighing the Scientific Consensus takes those tables and asks what the body of work actually supports, including where it splits. Questioning Your Own Sources is the counterweight, a set of habits for testing whether the papers you have gathered are the right ones and whether they say what you think they say. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans handles the wide opening move, mapping a field before you narrow, and Translating Between Disciplines is for reviews that cross fields, where the same term means different things and the methods do not line up. Read together they cover the full path from raw papers to a synthesis you can stand behind.
